key_insight: Plasma p-tau217 was elevated in both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and ALS, but its ratio to neurofilament light chain (NfL) distinguished the two better than p-tau217 alone.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest that elevated p-tau217 alone may not be specific to AD and that combining biomarkers could improve disease discrimination.
method: Measured baseline plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP in 551 participants across 10 diagnostic groups.
Compared biomarker levels and p-tau217-inferred amyloid positivity across groups.
Evaluated discrimination using ROC-AUC and explored clinical and longitudinal cognitive associations in ALS.
evidence_signal: The p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD with an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85–0.97), versus 0.65 (0.52–0.76) for p-tau217 alone.
watch_item: The reported discrimination comes from a primarily cross-sectional cohort analysis and requires independent validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
